title: Fused-silica grating through a chromium hard mask
summary: the photomask process: pattern the chromium, then let it hold the line
watch_for: Why the chromium is there at all. The fluorine etch takes resist about 30 times faster than chromium, so a resist mask would be gone long before the grating was deep — and the flanks stay steep because that chemistry has a vertical rate and no lateral one. Compare the chromium etch itself, which is a wet bath and undercuts its resist by as much as it etches down.

steps.note: 480 s at the table's 0.0833 nm/s is 40 nm of chromium.
Chlorine takes the chromium and leaves the glass at exactly zero.
Oxygen takes the resist and leaves both the chromium and the glass.
Fluorine cuts 200 nm of grating; the chromium loses about 8.
And the mask comes off in a bath that attacks nothing else.
